answer: Yes, it was. On August 21, 1911, Vincenzo Peruggia, an Italian who had worked at the Louvre, hid in the museum overnight, then took the Mona Lisa off the wall and walked out with it [1][2]. He kept it at his home in a trunk with a false bottom for about two years [2]. In late 1913 he offered it to Alfredo Geri, an art dealer in Florence, and said he wanted it returned to Italy. Italian police arrested him on December 12, 1913 [1][2]. The painting was shown briefly in Italy and went back to the Louvre in January 1914. The theft and all the press coverage helped make it the world's most famous painting [2][3].

sources.title: The Man Who Stole the Mona Lisa: What Happened to Vincenzo Peruggia?
The Heist that Made the Mona Lisa Famous
